An old Undo can erase a newer answer or edit

The notebook’s recording notice retains a complete old copy of the point. Its Undo can remain available after another operation has changed that point.

How it happens

  1. Record another slip for an existing verse from the notebook.
  2. Without dismissing the recording notice, open notebook practice and mark that verse forgotten. Close practice; no earlier recitation should be waiting to resume.
  3. Tap the original «إلغاء التسجيل» notice. The whole point is restored to its state before both actions.

Why it matters

The later practice failure and history disappear. The same stale snapshot can discard a note, reminder plan, or mistake edit made after the recording.

Recommended change

Bind Undo to the saved revision, or undo only the original event. At minimum, retire this Undo when a later mutation touches the same point.

Acceptance check Record → later edit or practice answer → Undo recording. The later operation survives, or the obsolete Undo is no longer offered.

Evidence, source excerpts & verification boundary

Reachable UI and repository path verified in current source. The destructive sequence was not exercised on the Pixel’s notebook.

B02P2Regression reproducedReminders

Spaced checks repeat in a later fresh-point reminder

A fresh slip due at a later reminder lets already-notified spaced checks re-enter the notification.

How it happens

  1. Let a spaced check be notified at an earlier slot, but leave it unanswered.
  2. At a later configured slot, have a fresh point become due.
  3. The new notification contains both the fresh point and the spaced check already notified that day.

Why it matters

Spaced checks can notify repeatedly on a day that is meant to notify them once. The notification’s contents disagree with the scheduler’s eligibility rules.

Recommended change

Build one eligible spaced-check list using both the slot’s prayer day and the last-notified day. Use that list for the guard, notification contents, and persisted reminder state.

Probe result
Expected posted IDs [20]; actual [10, 20].

Acceptance check With spaced point 10 already notified today and fresh point 20 now due, the later notification contains only 20.

Evidence, source excerpts & verification boundary

The real reminder method was invoked under Robolectric. Actual notification delivery and sound on the Pixel were not exercised.

B03P2Regression reproducedReminders

An Isha reminder after midnight can pull in the next day’s checks

The notification checks whether any old spaced check belongs to the reminder’s prayer day, then includes every spaced check due on the current calendar day.

How it happens

  1. An Isha reminder belonging to yesterday is delivered after midnight.
  2. Keep one spaced check due yesterday and another due today.
  3. Yesterday’s check admits the batch; today’s check is included too, before today’s own reminder slot.

Why it matters

A check can be announced earlier than the schedule promises. The source explicitly intends yesterday’s Isha to stay within yesterday’s checks.

Recommended change

Keep dueDay ≤ checksDay as a per-point filter when constructing the notification. Share the eligibility computation with B02.

Probe result
Expected posted IDs [10]; actual [10, 20].

Acceptance check For yesterday’s Isha, with point 10 due yesterday and point 20 due today, posted IDs are [10]. Add a separate case where today’s own slot legitimately rings with it.

Evidence, source excerpts & verification boundary

The real reminder method was tested with the prior-day Isha slot at 00:32. This is a notification-selection regression, not a live clock or alarm-delivery test.

B04P2Source traceLearning correctness

A resumed verse can keep an obsolete “last heard” time

Background audio deduplicates exposure by day and verse, without a time or playback-session boundary.

How it happens

  1. Start a single-verse Hifz listening clip and background the reader.
  2. Pause partway from the notification; leave the service alive for more than the 45-minute fresh-point gap.
  3. Resume the same verse, let it finish, then return to the reader. No different verse played in between.

Why it matters

The fresh point can be eligible immediately after hearing its answer: the delay still runs from the earlier exposure. This undermines the intended separation between listening and unaided recall.

Recommended change

Refresh exposure when sound actually resumes and when a new playback begins. Debounce repeated writes by time; do not suppress the same verse for the whole day.

Acceptance check After a long paused single-verse clip resumes in the background, its seen time advances. Returning after completion still delays that fresh question from the new exposure.

Evidence, source excerpts & verification boundary

Pause → resume → completion and the missed UI-observer path were traced in source. The 45-minute background scenario was not run on a device.

B05P2Regression reproducedState restoration

An unfinished review note disappears after restoration

Review counters and position are saved, but the open note’s point ID and text are omitted from the custom Saver.

How it happens

  1. After a failed review answer, open «أضف ملاحظة» and type a draft.
  2. Background the app and let Android recreate its activity/process with saved state.
  3. The review restores, but the note dialog and its text are gone.

Why it matters

The learner loses text they were in the middle of writing while the surrounding review appears to have recovered normally.

Recommended change

Add optional, backward-compatible note-draft fields to HifzReviewState.Saver and restore both the dialog and its text.

Probe result
Expected (42, Remember the differing ending); actual null.

Acceptance check A real Saver round-trip retains the draft (point 42, “Remember the differing ending”). Save and Cancel still clear it deliberately.

Evidence, source excerpts & verification boundary

The custom Saver round-trip fails reproducibly. Ordinary rotation is not the claimed reproduction: MainActivity handles orientation configuration changes.

B06P3Pixel 6 reproducedSearch

Numeric verse searches ignore surah/ayah order

The notebook treats a numeric reference as an unordered set of numbers rather than an exact Qur’an reference.

How it happens

  1. Open the notebook with a saved point at الملك، الآية 2 (67:2).
  2. Enter 2:67 in the search box.
  3. The result is still الملك، الآية 2, instead of an exact match for البقرة، الآية 67 or no result.

Why it matters

A precise-looking query returns the wrong reference. The record finder and notebook search do not interpret numeric references consistently.

Recommended change

Parse an explicit numeric reference before generic word matching, using the existing quranGoTo parser. Preserve broad text search for queries that are not explicit references.

Acceptance check 2:67 and 67:2 are distinct; Arabic digits and supported separators work consistently with the record finder.

Evidence, source excerpts & verification boundary

Reproduced on the Pixel 6’s installed development app and verified in current source. No notebook record was created or changed.

Explain practice consequences before starting

Before «راجع هذه المواضع», show how many selected points and related due questions will be asked. On each covered card, say whether this is a scheduled check or optional practice. The current explanation arrives after reveal; startPractice can add linked due questions outside the filter.

Acceptance check A learner can predict what advances the schedule before seeing the answer. Keep failure recording explicit.

I05Design recommendation

Make save and recovery failures visible

Publish repository state only after the atomic file commit succeeds, and give a retryable save error. If an unreadable notebook is moved to hifz.json.bad-*, explain the recovery state and offer export/recovery instead of presenting a silent empty notebook.

Acceptance check A simulated write failure leaves the prior saved state visible. A damaged or unsupported file is retained and explained without overwriting the recovery copy.

I06Design recommendation

Make reminder removal easy to target

The custom-time chip combines an editable chip with an 18dp clickable remove icon. Give removal a distinct accessible action and validate the effective hit target rather than relying on the icon’s appearance.

Acceptance check One-handed taps reliably remove the intended time; TalkBack announces the full time and action; the editor remains usable at large text sizes.

Inspected the installed development app, version 2.144 (155), updated on 23 October 2026. Matching version labels do not prove the APK is identical to the working tree. The search defect is corroborated by both the installed app and current source.

Data preservation verified. All three notebook records, including schedules and history, remained byte-for-byte identical. The exposure ledger and Hifz reminder preferences also matched exactly. Font scale was restored from the temporary 1.5× check to 1.15×; the notebook was returned to its All tab with an empty search.

No APK was installed, no review grade was submitted, and no record was created, edited, or deleted. Screens checked: home, notebook/search, reminder settings at normal and larger text. The device screenshots are embedded in this HTML.

Offline Gradle run under JDK 21, isolated build outputs. Kotlin compilation completed. These results cover selected Hifz logic and state tests, not the full application suite.

Audit probes: 3 expected failures

  • B02: already-notified spaced check re-enters a fresh reminder.
  • B03: prior-day Isha includes today’s check.
  • B05: unfinished note is lost by the real Saver.

These are additional regression probes outside application and committed test sources. They are evidence of defects, not a claim that the unchanged 78-test suite failed.

Current strengths to preserve

  • Home and notebook have separate entry points; the inspected home is compact.
  • Review state explicitly records assistance and defers questions whose answers were exposed.
  • Notebook practice distinguishes due checks from optional attempts and prevents duplicate answers on a card.
  • The exposure ledger merges background playback updates with stale UI snapshots; focused tests cover that merge.
  • Settings remained readable in the inspected 1.5× layout.

Still unverified

  • Real alarm delivery, notification sound, Doze/OEM behavior, and the after-midnight scenario on a physical device.
  • The 45-minute paused-background-audio scenario in B04.
  • TalkBack focus order, custom-time removal accuracy, and all review/correction layouts at large text.
  • Word-picker continuity when switching card/sheet layout and practice restoration before notebook loading completes.
  • Storage-failure recovery, calendar rollback during travel, and actual memorization outcomes.
